principles.statement: For penalty-aware TSP with carrot constraint, NN-guided 2-opt (choosing segment endpoints as spatially-close cities that are far apart in tour position) outperforms random 2-opt by a factor of ~2.3x in score (78.9 vs 33.5), because it focuses search on the most productive moves.
principles.regime: TSP with N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, 10% penalty at every 10th step for non-prime source cities
principles.mechanism: NN-guided 2-opt picks city pairs (a, b) where a and b are spatial neighbors but tour-order-distant. This targets exactly the crossings/detours that 2-opt can resolve. Random 2-opt wastes iterations on segments where both endpoints are already well-connected spatially.
principles.applicability_bounds: Requires precomputed K-nearest-neighbor lists (O(N log N) setup with grid). The benefit scales with N — at small N (<100), random 2-opt finds good moves quickly enough that NN guidance adds little.

principles.statement: For 2-opt on penalty-aware TSP, the cost delta can be computed in O(1 + segment_length/10) instead of O(segment_length): endpoint edge changes are O(1), and only penalty positions (every 10th step) inside the reversed segment need multiplier recomputation, because internal edge distances are conserved by reversal.
principles.regime: Any TSP variant where penalties apply at fixed step positions with multipliers on edge costs
principles.mechanism: When reversing segment [i..j], the set of edge distances inside the segment is the same (just in reverse order). Only the multipliers change because cities move to different step positions. Since multipliers only apply at every 10th step, only O(segment/10) positions need checking.
principles.applicability_bounds: Specific to this penalty structure (fixed-position multipliers). Does not apply to TSP variants where edge costs depend on visit order in other ways (e.g., time-dependent TSP).
